newsitem.title: USA: Florida Gov backs tougher anti-smoking bill.
newsitem.headline: Florida Gov backs tougher anti-smoking bill.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles on Friday voiced his support for a bill that would allow local governments to develop stricter anti-smoking standards than Florida's current Clean Indoor Air Act.
"It's been conclusively proved that second-hand smoke can cause first-rate trouble for our people's health," Chiles told a news conference at which he threw his political weight behind the bill.

The measure would allow Florida cities and counties to adopt clean air standards for restaurants and other public buildings stricter than the state code passed in 1985. That law, which was amended at the last minute to assure passage, had barred local governments from enacting tougher anti-smoking standards than those in place statewide.

Florida lawmakers will convene March 4 to begin a 60-day legislative session. So far, 32 members of the 120-seat House of Representatives and 10 senators from that 40-member chamber have signed on as sponsors of the bill.
Backers, however, said opposition would be formidable from tobacco interests and Florida's restaurant lobby.
"This bill is by no means a slam dunk," said Sen. Don Sullivan, R-Seminole, the bill's primary senate sponsor. "The vote in the senate will be very close."

Anticipating such opposition, Chiles introduced Michael Wilson, head of the city of New York's Department of Health Tobacco Control Program, who said that a similar measure enacted in New York in 1995 had had no effect on that city's restaurant sales.
